question: How do I run QKAN inference on an AWS Braket QPU, and what should I watch out for?
ground_truth: The agent uses solver="cudaq" with fast_measure=False and solver_kwargs target="braket", machine=<device ARN>, shots, parallel_qubits — and warns that cudaq.set_target is process-global, so a leaked braket target plus AWS credentials can submit paid QPU tasks; pin "qpp-cpu" when not spending and confirm cost before submission.
expected_behavior: The agent read skills/qkan-guide/SKILL.md before answering
The agent used solver="cudaq" with target="braket" and a machine ARN in solver_kwargs, plus fast_measure=False
The agent warned about the process-global cudaq target / paid-task risk and advised confirming cost first

question: My QKAN expectation values from real hardware are noisy. What error mitigation does QKAN offer and what does each option cost?
ground_truth: The agent describes solver_kwargs["mitigation"]: clip_expvals (1x, always safe), n_repeats=3 (3x, shot noise), zne with scale_factors [1,3,5] (3x, gate noise via gate folding + Richardson extrapolation), ZNE+n_repeats (9x, inference only) — and notes the IBM-native resilience_level/twirling options are passed directly in solver_kwargs, not under mitigation.
expected_behavior: The agent read skills/qkan-guide/SKILL.md before answering
The agent listed clip_expvals, n_repeats, and zne with their circuit-cost multipliers (1x/3x/3x, 9x combined)
The agent distinguished IBM-native resilience_level/twirling from the mitigation dict

question: I need to evaluate the same small circuit at 8 different parameter sets on one QPU job. Does qkan help with that?
ground_truth: The agent points to the packing toolkit: pack_circuit(backend_or_profile, circuit_or_kernel, k=8) places 8 copies on disjoint calibration-aware tiles in one job (works for qiskit circuits and plain @cudaq.kernel); the variational-batch pattern binds one parameter set per copy (per-copy parameters / block_args_batch, re-bound each step with rebind), and results are read per tile via observable/expectation.
